page.title: Day 2 against Neave's manual
page.standfirst_html: Every flag the comparator raised for Day 2, adjudicated against E.Day.2.12Oct21.pdf — the extracted text for wording, 39 page images, the PDF's own font data for every italic and bold run, and a word- and punctuation-level diff of the whole day. Two sentences on the live site say the opposite of the source. Technical Aid 3 warns that the Red Beads σ formula does not apply to other kinds of data; a LaTeX \emph{} that Pandoc silently drops means production reads “does apply”. And the Postscript's story is reversed: the Foreman told the second Madrid team about their predecessors' awful results, not “far better” ones, and a nonsense fragment — “Regrettably a production.” — stands where Neave says the slur was perceived. Two whole passages are missing (the Foreman's commentary on the statisticians' first week, which leaves a lower-case fragment on the page, and the day's closing lines), Activity 2–g is labelled as a second Pause for Thought 2–e, the Out-of-hours note names the wrong Major Activity and the wrong Day 3 page, and two anchors send readers returning from the Appendix five and two pages back. Four site-written chart and table descriptions state wrong numbers, and two of them answer a Pause for Thought before it is asked. Twenty-five emphasis findings, none of which any flag can see.

sections.title: Fix proposed
sections.note_html: Ordered by source page. Thirteen are marked critical: two meaning reversals live in production (D2-20, D2-32), a word Pandoc deletes (D2-19), an invented fragment (D2-34), two missing passages (D2-25, D2-30), a wrong activity label (D2-26), a wrong Major Activity and a wrong page (D2-37, D2-38), two misnamed anchors (D2-24, D2-28), chart data missing a month (D2-03), and two site descriptions that answer a Pause for Thought early (D2-08, D2-11). D2-01, D2-08, D2-11 and D2-33 are site-written accessibility text, not transcription — accept or leave on that basis.

items.flag: Unsourced 5 · 17%
items.source_html: The run chart beside Neave's paragraph: high through August, a steep fall through September, a sharp recovery at the start of October, a jump at the start of November, and an abrupt drop at the start of December.
items.site_html: Alt text: “values <mark class='gone'>declining from around 1000 in August to approximately 400 by December, with sharp drops in October and November</mark>”. Description: “starts near 1000 in August, <mark class='gone'>dips slightly through September, then drops sharply in October and again in November</mark>, ending close to 400 by December.”
items.evidence_html: The chart image (Picture 1.jpg, the source's own figure) was enlarged and read directly. Both site-written texts describe a different chart: September is the steepest fall, not a slight dip; October and November both rise; the drop is at the start of December; and the line ends near 500, not 400. A screen-reader user is told the opposite of what a sighted reader sees. This is site-authored accessibility text, not transcription, so it is yours to accept or leave — but it states facts about the source that are wrong.

Although the story met with mixed reactions, he was sure that the information would prove to be highly motivational for the new team—they would strive to do better in order to restore national pride.

sections.title: Out of scope for a per-day pass
sections.note_html: Real, but a per-day transcription pass is the wrong tool. S-01 is a defect class the comparator cannot see, with eight live instances on closed Day 1 — “Do it here” is a reasonable answer for that one.

items.flag: Never flagged — found by grepping for D2-27's shape across the corpus
items.source_html: Words Neave hyphenates only at a line end: “Con-gress”, “Man-agement”, “suc-cess”, “read-ing”, “con-firm”, “speci-fic”, “success-fully”, and the compound “many-stringed”.
items.site_html: Eight on Day 1 render with a stray space — the built page shows “Trades Union Con- gress” (day-01/08-attraction.qmd:128), plus 06-outline.qmd:120, 125, 04-resources.qmd:80, 03-statistics.qmd:26, 143, 156, 07-quality-theory.qmd:132.
items.evidence_html: A .qmd line ending in letters- followed by a line break: Markdown joins the lines with a space and keeps the hyphen. The comparator cannot see this class: #740 joins hyphen wraps symmetrically on both sides, so “Con- gress” in the site and “Con- gress” in pdftotext normalise to the same word. A corpus grep ([A-Za-z]{2}-$) finds exactly nine: these eight and D2-27. Day 1 is closed; accept to hand on, or choose “Do it here” to fix all eight in this PR alongside D2-27.
items.outcome: Done here, per the decision: all eight Day 1 hard-wrapped hyphens joined (03-statistics.qmd ×3, 04-resources.qmd, 06-outline.qmd ×2, 07-quality-theory.qmd, 08-attraction.qmd), keeping the real compound “many-stringed”. The corpus grep [A-Za-z]{2}-$ now finds none.

items.chip: Note refers to an absent page
items.source_html: Neave's small print on printed p9: “<mark class='src'>Referring back to my comment on the reverse of today’s ID page</mark>, the distortion was particularly bad on this recruitment advertisement.”
items.site_html: Transcribed word for word — but the site has no ID page, so there is no comment to refer back to (the note is X-01's front matter).
items.evidence_html: Correctly transcribed, so not a fix; but a reader meets a reference to something that is not there. Two honest options: a deviation entry recording that the ID-page note is omitted, or a short editorial bracket. Either is an editorial call for the deviations log rather than a transcription change, so handed on rather than decided inside this pass.
items.decision_note: my preference: a deviation entry recording that the ID-page note is omitted
items.outcome: Neave’s note kept word for word; the omission of the ID page’s reverse-side note it refers to is logged in docs/deviations/2026-09-17-day-02-id-page-note-omitted.md.

items.chip: Link lands inside a collapsed reveal
items.source_html: “…typified by all the discussion in the so-called “Analysis” of the results on pages 12 and 13. So, … go back and re-read that page and a half before continuing here.”
items.site_html: [pages 12 and 13, starting in A Brief Overview](03-a-brief-overview.qmd#sec-page12), where #sec-page12 is inside Pause for Thought 2–d's <div class="collapse"> (03:74–75).
items.evidence_html: The anchor's element is hidden until its button is pressed, so a reader following Neave's bolded instruction lands on a page with nothing visible at the target. An interaction problem, not a transcription one — the fix is either to move the anchor to just above the reveal button or to open the collapse on hash navigation. Hand on.
items.decision_note: I'd like us to move the anchor to just above the reveal button
items.outcome: Done here, per the note: []{#sec-page12} moved out of the collapse to just above Pause for Thought 2–d’s reveal button.
